supported_scope: Commands, filesystem paths, external services (MCP tools), and network destinations (URLs) can be limited by fine-grained allow, deny, and ask permission rules configured in Antigravity CLI settings and managed interactively.
required_setup: Configure permission rules in ~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/settings.json or interactively via /permissions command; optionally enable terminal sandbox and set toolPermission mode for sandbox enforcement.
constraints: Permissions follow action(target) format with allow, deny, and ask lists.
Unconfigured actions default to Ask mode with secure fallbacks.
Terminal sandbox restricts commands and network access unless unsandboxed rules apply.
Approval prompts appear inline in /agents panel or as interactive TUI prompt cards.
Scope editing of file and URL targets is supported in prompts except for terminal commands.

evidence.section: Agent permissions > Antigravity CLI > CLI fine-grained permissions
evidence.quote: Antigravity CLI integrates a robust fine-grained permissions engine. Every sensitive operation the agent performs is represented as a permission resource formatted as action(target). Permissions are evaluated across three distinct access lists configured inside your global settings (~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/settings.json): deny, ask, allow.
evidence.claim: Fine-grained permission engine built in with deny, ask, and allow lists.

evidence.section: Terminal sandbox > Antigravity CLI > CLI permissions integration
evidence.quote: The sandbox derives its access boundaries from your Permissions configuration: Filesystem: Workspace folders and paths allowed under write_file are mounted read-write. Paths allowed under read_file are mounted read-only. Denied paths are blocked, and everything else is inaccessible. Network: Sandboxed commands run without network access by default. evidence.claim: Sandbox enforces filesystem and network restrictions based on permissions.

evidence.section: Agents command (/agents) > Subagent monitoring and control > Inline tool approvals
evidence.quote: If a subagent attempts a protected operation (such as modifying a file or running a shell command in a sandboxed environment), the authorization prompt displays inline in the /agents panel. You can press A to approve or D to deny directly from the list.
evidence.claim: Inline approval prompts for protected operations in /agents panel.

evidence.section: Agent permissions > Antigravity CLI > Supported CLI actions and matching rules
evidence.quote: Fine-grained permissions follow a standard schema pattern: action(target). The supported actions, target format specifications, and matching algorithms are listed in the following table: read_file, write_file, read_url, execute_url, command, unsandboxed, mcp. Defaults fallback to Ask.
evidence.claim: Supported actions cover commands, files, URLs, and MCP tools with matching rules.
